content: The following adverse effects and considerations are associated with the use of this medication: Hypotension occurs in approximately 3% of patients. Gastrointestinal disorders, such as constipation and gastritis, have been reported in 1% of patients. Laboratory investigations may reveal increased alanine aminotransferase levels. Metabolism and nutrition disorders, including hypokalemia, have been observed. Nervous system disorders, such as dizziness, may occur. Renal and urinary disorders, including hematuria, have been reported. Respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal disorders, such as dyspnea, may develop. Patients with known hypersensitivity to any aminoglycoside should avoid this medication. Refer to the Black Box Warnings for additional safety information: 1. Nephrotoxicity has been reported, with most cases involving serum creatinine increases of ≥1 mg/dL above baseline. These changes were generally reversible. 2. Aminoglycosides have been associated with exacerbation of muscle weakness in patients with underlying neuromuscular disorders or delayed recovery of neuromuscular function in those receiving concomitant neuromuscular blocking agents. 3. Fetal harm may occur if administered to pregnant women. There is no available data on the use of this drug in pregnant women to assess the risk of adverse developmental outcomes. 4. Serious and occasionally fatal hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported in patients receiving aminoglycoside antibacterial drugs. Treatment should be discontinued immediately if an allergic reaction occurs. Prescribing this drug in the absence of a confirmed or strongly suspected bacterial infection is unlikely to benefit the patient and increases the risk of developing drug-resistant bacteria. Regarding use during pregnancy and breastfeeding: There is no data on the presence of this drug in human milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. However, the drug has been detected in rat milk. When considering use during breastfeeding, weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant or the underlying maternal condition. Preparation and administration guidelines: Vials do not contain preservatives. Use appropriate aseptic techniques when preparing the infusion solution. Discard any unused portion of the vial. Inspect parenteral drug products for particulate matter and discoloration prior to administration, if the solution and container allow. Administer the infusion over 30 minutes. Unused vials should be refrigerated at 2–8°C (36–46°F). Diluted solutions are stable at room temperature for up to 24 hours. This information is provided for general educational purposes. For the most current formulary information, contact the applicable plan provider.
